task: Synthetic binary spatial-cluster identity: which of two neighboring source clusters along probe y is more active in a 100 ms window, with label-independent tonic sources along the shank
split: contiguous first-N train after seeded generation; same indices for both models
forward_model: edge.forward.render_recording: quasi-static point-monopole voltages with a triphasic kernel (not LFPy/MEArec morphology)

baseline.features: 32 unsigned per-channel spike counts from forward-model peak channels

spatial.features: 32 counts concatenated with 8 probe-y occupancy bins and mean estimated xyz_um

neuropixels.task: blank (0) versus full (1) right-side visual contrast
neuropixels.neural_features: first 32 VISp units, counts from 50-250 ms after stimulus onset
neuropixels.limitation: Processed spike counts, not raw probe voltage. Spatial localization features are off because this extract has no per-spike xyz in probe_um. Visual stimulus labels are not perceptions or intended movement. Fixture sorted spikes were not treated as voltages.

rtl_count_baseline: rtl/spike_count_decoder.sv remains the 32-count RTL baseline and was not modified
limitations: Synthetic labels mark which simulated source cluster was rate-modulated; they are not perceptions.
This experiment is not vision restoration, not intended-movement decoding, and not a claim about humans.
edge.forward.render_recording: quasi-static point-monopole voltages with a triphasic kernel (not LFPy/MEArec morphology)
Localization uses an amplitude engine; failures fall back to observed peak-channel contact geometry, never source truth.
Spatial improvement is reported only if held-out accuracy rose on the same split; it is not assumed.
Neuropixels CCF coordinates are not human neuron coordinates and were not mapped through edge.coords.
